deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page holds Riemann's numerical work on the zeta function at t/2π ≈ 3.29 and 10, with values of ϑ/π. This page is a sheet of heuristic scratch work on the prime-counting problem. It reads as a sketch of how the density 1/log x of the primes is reflected in the pole of ζ(s) at s=1.

(1) Definition and Euler product. ζ(s) = 1 + 2^{-s} + 3^{-s} + ... = Σ n^{-s} = Π_p 1/(1-p^{-s}). The isolated note 1/(s-1) records the polar part of ζ at s=1. The note 1/log x in the margin is the conjectured density of the primes.

(2) Taking logarithms. log ζ(s) = -Σ_p log(1-p^{-s}) = Σ_p p^{-s} + (1/2) Σ_p p^{-2s} + (1/3) Σ_p p^{-3s} + .... Riemann writes Σ log(1-(1/p)^s) = -Σ(1/p)^s ± (1/2) Σ p^{-2s}, the start of the series log(1-u) = -u - u²/2 - ....

(3) Model integrals. ∫_a^∞ dx/x^s = a^{1-s}/(s-1) for Re s > 1. Writing x^{-s} = e^{-s log x}, he considers ∫ (1/log x) dx/x^s. Differentiating in s gives -∫ x^{-s} dx = -a^{1-s}/(s-1). Hence (my fill-in) ∫_a^∞ x^{-s} dx/log x = -log(s-1) + regular function near s=1. With t = log x it equals E1((s-1) log a).

Compare this with log ζ(s) ~ -log(s-1) ~ Σ_p p^{-s}. The sum over primes behaves like ∫ x^{-s} dx/log x, i.e. the primes have density 1/log x. This is what 'log(1-s) = ∫ (1/log x) dx/x^s' expresses, up to sign and a constant.

The crossed attempt '1/log(1-s) = ∫ f(x) dx/x^s' is a generic Mellin-inversion ansatz. It seeks a density f whose Mellin transform reproduces a given function of s.

The line e^{-s log x}/log x · 1/(1-s) + ... is the start of integration by parts of ∫ x^{-s}/log x dx. Its antiderivative is x^{1-s}/((1-s) log x) + (1/(1-s)) ∫ x^{-s}/(log x)² dx.

(4) The logarithmic integral and its expansion. θ(x) := ∫_a^x dx/log x = ∫ dx/log x + C, i.e. Li(x) up to a constant. Integration by parts gives ∫ dx/(log x)^m = x/(log x)^m + m ∫ dx/(log x)^{m+1}. The page carries the terms x(1/log x)^m and x(1/log x)^{m+1}, with a line linking them. It ends in the asymptotic series θ(x) = x/log x + x/log²x + 2! x/log³x + ..., written as x/log x + x/log x² + ....

(5) The crossed 1·2···p and Π(p), then x, (1·2···p)+1. This is Euclid's argument that 1·2···p + 1 has a prime factor larger than p, so the primes are infinite in number.

(6) The crossed 1/y, 1/(x-y), then ∫_a^x (1/log(x-y))(1/log y) dy. This is the additive convolution of the prime density with itself. Heuristically it is the expected number of representations of x as a sum of two primes, i.e. a naive Goldbach-type count without arithmetic correction factor. It may alternatively be an exploratory convolution of densities; the page gives no further context. The next page begins Π(1-1/p) and a Möbius-type sum 1 - 1/2 - 1/3 + 1/5 + 1/6 - 1/7.
errors: The second term of -Σ log(1-p^{-s}) carries the wrong sign as drawn: log(1-u) = -u - u²/2 - ..., so Σ log(1-p^{-s}) = -Σ p^{-s} - (1/2) Σ p^{-2s} - .... The '+1/2' is a slip, or a misreading of an overwritten sign.

'log(1-s) = ∫ (1/log x) dx/x^s' holds only asymptotically near s=1, up to sign and an additive regular function. Exactly, ∫_a^∞ x^{-s}/log x dx = E1((s-1) log a) = -log(s-1) - log log a - γ + O(s-1). The argument 1-s is negative for s>1, so the log needs interpretation.

In the integration-by-parts step for ∫ dx/(log x)^m the factor m is not visible. The correct identity is ∫ dx/(log x)^m = x/(log x)^m + m ∫ dx/(log x)^{m+1}. This makes the coefficients of the series k!, not 1.
The line 'θ(x)/x = 1/log x + x/log x + ...' is dimensionally inconsistent as transcribed. The intended statement is θ(x) = x/log x + ∫ dx/(log x)², or θ(x)/x = 1/log x + 1/log²x + ....
The convolution ∫_a^x dy/(log y log(x-y)) has a singular endpoint at y=x (log(x-y) → 0 at y = x-1, and the integrand is singular there). The upper limit should be x-a.

deep.surprise_reason: Almost everything is routine background to the 1859 paper: the Euler product, log ζ, the density 1/log x seen through ∫ x^{-s} dx/log x, the Li expansion and Euclid. The one mildly notable item is the additive convolution ∫ dy/(log y log(x-y)). If it is a Goldbach heuristic, it would predate Sylvester's 1871 heuristic, but the page is too fragmentary to be sure of the intent.

transcription_corrections: The 'x' crossed out near the top left appears to be the start of 'Σ' or 'π'. The line reads (crossed) x + log x, then x + log x, probably first-order guesses for prime-counting approximations.
'∫_a^∞ ∂x/x^s = a^{1-s}/(s-1)': the image shows a leading '+' and an exponent like 'a^{1-s}'. Consistent.
'-Σ(1/p)^s + 1/2 Σ 1/p^{2s}': the sign before 1/2 is unclear in the image. The mathematically correct sign is '-'.
'e^{-log x s}' line: the image shows 'e^{-log x s}' with an attached ', -∂s' (differentiation in s), not '[?]'.
'θ(x)/x = 1/log x + x/log x...' is better read as θ(x) = x/log x + ... + ∫ ∂x/(log x)², with '(1/log x)^{m+1} log x' as an intermediate term of the integration by parts.
'log(1-s)' on the left of the crossed integral matches the image: '(log(1-s)) = ∫ (1/log x) ∂x/x^s'.
